phase1_assignment.objective: Audit generic scientist-agent evidence packaging, reproducibility and handoff mechanisms that preserve observation/inference/uncertainty and exact continuation.

observations.mechanism: the public pre-submission EvoScientist release is not by itself an evaluated-IVE implementation fingerprint because the host revision delegates IVE to an optional external skill that is neither bundled nor pinned
observations.evidence: Official tag v.0.0.1-rc.1 resolves to commit 388519755987256cbd0ecf4cd28d31b2c06fa2ea and was published 2026-03-08. At that tag, EvoScientist/prompts.py directs failed experiment pipelines to run /skills/evo-memory/SKILL.md if installed and otherwise to update memory manually. pyproject.toml does not pin EvoSkills/evo-memory as a dependency, and the bundled EvoScientist/skills directory contains only find-skills and skill-creator. Therefore the host release revision cannot alone identify the exact IVE mechanism bytes used by the paper evaluation.
observations.scope: This establishes a public reproducibility/provenance gap for the release surface. It does not prove the authors lacked an internal exact evaluation environment or that no other public artifact binds the evaluated external skill revision.

observations.mechanism: PRAXIS isolates adaptive retrieval quality but not receiver-side authorization to enforce retrieved negative memory
observations.evidence: PRAXIS reports a 110-case retrieval benchmark comparing BM25, tag/tool Jaccard, naive/weighted RRF and adaptive retrieval. Adaptive retrieval reaches recall@10 0.683 versus BM25 0.646 (reported p=0.009) and uses agent/task metadata, toolchain and negative/inapplicable markers. However the gold target for each query is another case from the same domain agent, so this experiment evaluates retrieval relevance within domain rather than whether a retrieved negative case is safe to adopt as a target constraint. Searches of the paper found no isolated reviewer-gate or target-side revalidation ablation; reviewer gating remains component-confounded with the full system.
observations.scope: Direct evidence for task-aware/adaptive retrieval under the paper's same-domain gold definition; not causal evidence that target-side applicability/revalidation improves scientific correctness or transfer safety.

inferences.proposal: Failure-memory provenance should bind the handoff claim to the immutable source artifact digest, exact implementation revision and mechanism fingerprint. A host-repository commit or near-date release is insufficient when the operative mechanism lives in an optional/unpinned external skill or repository.

Retrieval success, same-domain similarity, or stored boundary metadata may select a candidate memory but may not authorize pruning/FORBID/constraint use. Any action-set narrowing requires explicit receiver-side target-applicability evidence that is current, available and not contradicted or superseded.

new_invariants: exact source artifact/implementation revision/mechanism fingerprint binding
domain-general prequalification policy-revision binding and explicit revocation
evidence-registry revision binding plus supersession invalidation
mandatory receiver-side target-applicability check before constraint/pruning use
failure_memory_v2.local_test_result: 15/15 expected semantic outcomes passed; all 15 mutated records were Draft 2020-12 schema-valid before semantic validation

unverified_claims: No explicit public artifact was found in this run that binds the published EvoScientist evaluation to an exact external evo-memory/EvoSkills revision; absence from the inspected public release surface is not proof that no such artifact exists elsewhere or internally.

PRAXIS directly isolates adaptive retrieval and negative-case memory effects at their reported scopes, but no isolated target-side reviewer/revalidation intervention was found in the inspected paper; causal credit for that gate remains unresolved.
The v2 validator is a role-local protocol probe, not evidence that its new gates improve scientific-agent benchmark performance; those causal effects still require matched evaluation.

base_continuation_preserved.note: Base continuation remains frozen while the Phase-1 overlay is active; it was not resumed or semantically expanded.

termination_diagnostics.blocker: Exact evaluated external-skill revision provenance for EvoScientist remains unresolved, and PRAXIS does not isolate receiver-side applicability/revalidation as a causal component. V2 protocol gates are executable local probes but still lack matched scientist-agent performance ablation.
termination_diagnostics.termination_cause: Invocation checkpoint/time boundary with a nonempty Phase-1 frontier. Repository main advanced due to role-local artifact writes, but revision21 identity checks confirmed frozen DESIRED_STATE and scientist_agents config blobs were unchanged, so this was not treated as semantic-control termination.

If the Phase-1 evidence-handoff assignment remains active: (1) inspect the exact Mar-8 EvoSkills lineage and paper/data-availability artifacts for any explicit evaluated-revision pin or self-describing mechanism fingerprint connecting arXiv 2603.08127 to evo-memory, while preserving the public-gap boundary if none exists; (2) inspect PRAXIS supplementary/raw artifacts for an isolated reviewer, applicability-filter or target-side revalidation intervention and raw fixed outputs, preserving the attribution boundary if absent; (3) extend v2 with an adversarial case where retrieval/same-domain relevance is positive but target_applicability is absent and therefore constraint use must fail, plus a multi-repository dependency-pin mismatch case where the host revision is fixed but the external skill revision drifts; (4) seek a matched scientist-agent experiment that ablates target-side applicability/revalidation itself; (5) only then retry Duke trapped-ion file-level source access.
